source.title: Finite-sample analysis of interpolating linear classifiers in the overparameterized regime
source.authors: Niladri S. Chatterji; Philip M. Long

page_placements.theme: Arbitrary-label fitting extends beyond standard deep networks

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests interpolation and generalization with label noise for overparameterized maximum-margin linear classifiers, an extension to a different model class from the deep networks in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper studies linear classifiers, not standard deep networks. Its results therefore do not test any listed version as worded. The introduction cites Zhang et al. (2017), but those cited results are not this paper's own results.
record.test_reason: The study proves bounds and reports simulations for maximum-margin linear classifiers, whereas all six versions concern deep networks. Its noisy-label interpolation results address a related question but test no listed version. Zhang et al. is cited as motivation.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. More precisely, the authors show that maximum-margin linear classification, corresponding to the limiting direction of gradient descent on unregularized logistic or exponential loss, can achieve nearly optimal population risk despite bounded label noise under their distributional and overparameterization assumptions.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes maximum-margin linear classifiers; it does not reproduce the deep-network experiments in the original sources. It relates this classifier to the large-time limit of gradient descent on exponential or logistic loss for separable data.
record.method_sensitivity: Population-risk bounds depend on p, ||μ||, η, and the stated distributional and sample-size assumptions. In simulations, test error varies with p, s, and γ.

fits_no_version.finding: Under stated distributional, signal and dimension assumptions, maximum-margin linear classification has population error bounded by η + exp(−c||μ||⁴/p). Boolean simulations report zero training error on every run at label-flip probabilities 0.05 or 0.1, with test error depending on dimension and signal sparsity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sufficiently overparameterized maximum-margin linear classifiers can interpolate partially corrupted labels while approaching the noise-level population error under suitable signal and distribution conditions.

record.problems: The experiments use synthetic Boolean data and a linear classifier, not deep networks or fully random labels. The simulation plots provide no numerical test-error values in the text, and no uncertainty intervals are stated for the simulated test errors.

untested.parts: Deep-network fitting of completely random labels, chance test error, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Relative training time for true versus random labels and convergence slowdown with increasing corruption.
Deep-network fitting of shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels and Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect deep-network training fit and steadily increasing test error across a label-corruption sweep from none to all.
Effects of weight decay, dropout and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization in deep networks.
Deep-network learning order for real patterns versus noisy labels. The bounded per-example loss ratios proved here concern linear classifiers and do not measure that learning order.

record.verdict_notes: States are assessed against the listed claim versions. None of the rows measures the specified deep-network behavior; cannot_determine does not negate the reported linear-classifier results.

versions.untested_parts: Deep networks; completely random labeling; test error at chance.
Training-time comparison and convergence speed as corruption increases.
Shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
A sweep from no corrupted labels to all labels corrupted and the resulting test-error trajectory.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation on fitting random labels or true-label generalization.
Learning order for real versus noisy or random labels over training.

source_check.correct: Theorem 4 additionally requires the Section 2 distributional assumptions: balanced clean labels; x = Uq + ỹμ with U unitary and q having independent, zero-mean, sub-Gaussian coordinates of norm at most 1; E||q||² ≥ κp; P and P̃ have the same covariate marginal.
